resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 7,930 ft (2,417 m) and FirelookOut gives 8,015 ft. The record keeps the NHLR figure of 2,417 m because it is the one with a metric value; the sources do not say which is more accurate.

notes_for_editor: NHLR and FirelookOut share nearly the same wording, so the 1923, 1925 and 1962 dates rest mainly on one text, with the 1962 date backed by the independent 2022 magazine article. No NRHP nomination or Forest Service document was found or read. The access level is unknown: staffed in summer and reached by trail, but no source says whether the cab is open to visitors. The brief's record checked out on coordinates, elevation (within the NHLR figure), and the 1962 build date; no corrections. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the story's window wording now reads fragile piece, to match the 2022 magazine quote; the summit wording now reads lookout site, because the sources say here; and the visitor-access sentence no longer carries a footnote, since no cited source addresses it.
